synthesis:draft.headline: Peak five-minute RRP in NSW1 was 531.84849 $/MWh at 2026-07-31 07:30 AEST (interval end 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z).
summary: The peak five-minute RRP for NSW1 was 531.84849 $/MWh at interval end 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z (2026-07-31 07:30 AEST) [ev0440].
Fourteen five-minute intervals met the analysis threshold of 300.0 $/MWh during the window [ev0876]; the analysis threshold is 300.0 $/MWh [ev0878].
Dispatch TOTALDEMAND at the five-minute peak interval (interval end 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z) was 11432.7 MW [ev0441].
Dispatch NETINTERCHANGE at the same five-minute peak interval was -1144.98 MW (net flow into NSW1 / import) [ev0442].

Operational demand for the half-hour containing the price extreme (half-hour ending 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z) was 11178.0 MW (operational demand, 30-minute measure) [ev0903]; the window maximum operational demand was 11382.0 MW (half-hour ending 2026-07-30T10:00:00Z) [ev0880].

AEMO published a market notice reporting a planned outage of Directlink that covered the date in question: "A planned outage of Directlink all 3 cables in the NSW region was scheduled from 0700 hrs 27/07/2026 to 1700 hrs 31/07/2026." [c1].

possible_explanations.statement: The planned outage of Directlink reported in the market notice [c1] may have reduced interconnector import capability into NSW1 and so might be related to the price spike.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Obtain Directlink-specific flow and capability records and pre/post outage transfer limits for the interval ending 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z and check AEMO constraint binding logs (SOLVEDCONSTRAINTS) for that interval to see whether import capability was reduced or constraints were binding.

possible_explanations.statement: A tight local supply/demand balance (high dispatch TOTALDEMAND at the five-minute peak and high operational demand in the containing half-hour) might have contributed to the price spike.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Examine unit availability and outage records, generator offer and rebid submissions and the dispatch merit order around interval 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z to see whether insufficient low-cost generation was available to meet dispatch TOTALDEMAND at that interval.

possible_explanations.statement: Rapid changes in individual unit outputs or dispatchable resource behaviour might have coincided with the spike (e.g. large generator output changes observed in the surrounding hours).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Inspect 5-minute DUID-level dispatch traces and offer prices for the minutes before and after 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z to identify units that set price and whether their offers or changes in output aligned with the timing of the spike.

citations.quote: A planned outage of Directlink all 3 cables in the NSW region was scheduled from 0700 hrs 27/07/2026 to 1700 hrs 31/07/2026.
citations.supports: reports a planned outage of Directlink covering the investigated date

uncertainties: Dispatch and notice records are observational; they do not by themselves establish a causal relationship between the Directlink planned outage and the price spike.

Netinterchange is an aggregate regional net flow and does not identify per-interconnector flows; the available netinterchange value does not show whether Directlink specifically was carrying imports at the time.
missing_evidence: Interconnector-specific flow and capability data for Directlink (per-interconnector SCADA/limits) for interval ending 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z and surrounding intervals.
AEMO constraint binding logs / SOLVEDCONSTRAINTS for NSW1 around 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z showing which constraints were binding and which set the marginal price.
Generator offer and rebid submissions and the identity of the price-setting unit(s) for the five-minute interval ending 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z.
Detailed unit outage/availability notices that would show whether local generation was unavailable at the time.
